$comment: States a format that is already in use; changes nothing in it. Source: adcut's adcut/contracts.py (contract B) and the video-ads skill pack's docs/contract.md (which writes it, with the stage words and the delivery rule). A TSV contract: the schema describes one row, each cell is text; a blank cell of a column that is not in 'required' is unknown, never 0.
title: ads.results/1
description: An ad platform's results: one row per creative, date range, plan and placement, the facts as the platform gave them, with whether the days are complete and settled. An operator writes one file a day (the whole picture as of that moment: every creative still running; a creative missing from it is unknown, not 0); makers and measurement read it.
x-producer: an operator (video-ads: Meta, 千川, 腾讯广告; any operator may)
x-rules: The first line is '# ads.results/1'; the old mark '# cads.results/1' is refused by adcut's reader and still read by the video-ads skill pack's.
nk is unique in the file.
A fission needs its scored_at; a scored_at without a fission is read and kept out.
A row whose creative is still running is in every file; a creative missing from a file is unknown, not 0.
A word outside the stage and stage_reason vocabularies is read, kept and warned about, never refused: the vocabulary is the operator's to grow.
A later version only adds columns at the end.

creative_code.description: The creative's code as the manifest gave it, check digit included.

platform.description: The platform id, as in ads.creatives/1.

account.description: The platform account the row belongs to.

ref_kind.description: Which kind of id the platform filed the row under; ref_value is that id.

ref_value.description: The id the row was filed under, as text.

unit_id.description: The plan or ad unit in the row's key, when the platform has one.

placement.description: Where the ad ran, when the platform splits by placement.

date_from.description: First day the row covers, YYYY-MM-DD.

date_to.description: Last day the row covers, YYYY-MM-DD; not before date_from.

nk.description: The producer's hash of the row's natural key (platform, account, ref_kind, ref_value, plan, placement, period): a row id for the reader, nothing more.

exported_at.description: When the file's row was exported: ISO 8601 with its zone.

complete.description: 1 when the platform has given every day the row covers.

settled.description: 1 when the numbers no longer move (千川's orders settle in 7 days); a reader never takes an unsettled day's orders for final.

restated.description: 1 when the platform changed numbers it had given for these days earlier.

conversions.description: Conversions of the goal the operator's agent chose, whatever it is.

gmv_cny.description: Order value in CNY, as exported.

net_conversions.description: Conversions net of refunds, where the platform gives them; carried, not read by adcut.

net_gmv_cny.description: Order value in CNY net of refunds, where the platform gives it; carried, not read by adcut.

play_3s_rate.description: Share of plays that reached 3 seconds, as exported.

completion_rate.description: Share of plays watched to the end, as exported.

cpa_cny.description: Cost per conversion in CNY, as exported.

stage.description: The creative's lifecycle stage, one of x-vocabulary.stage; blank until the operator's lifecycle has judged it.

verdict.description: A platform review's verdict on the material; blank until the operator reads it.

verdict_reason.description: The reason that came with the verdict; blank with it.

fission.description: Optional, last. The operator's one evaluation of the creative, 0.00 to 1.00: how much it wants to keep fissioning (its neighbours, one dimension swapped, cover more of the traffic). Not a conversion count. 0.5 is the account's median creative. Blank is unknown, never 0. A creative's score changes over time: a later file carries a new fission with a new scored_at.

scored_at.description: Optional, with fission. When the fission was computed: ISO 8601 with its zone.

stage_reason.description: Optional, last. Why the row's stage is what it is, one of x-vocabulary.stage_reason (low_reach: the platform never showed it, change the concept or the opening; no_conversion: shown, nobody bought, change the offer or the page).
